synoptic.summary: A weak trough that split off the Montana system is sliding south of Utah toward northern Mexico, and a broad Pacific ridge is building over the top: dry, no convection, light terrain-driven winds through the weekend. Friday a northerly pressure gradient keeps north flow at Point of the Mountain all day — no south drainage this morning, which breaks the usual pattern. Saturday looks like a textbook ridge day (light south drainage in the morning, switch to north around 14:00). Sunday the forecast turns south-southeast all day with no afternoon switch to north — another departure from the normal cycle. The winds-aloft download failed for all three forecast times, so rotor checks rely only on the NWS mixed-layer (transport) wind.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: With the presence of the ridge, winds will be generally light and terrain driven. However, the combination of a northerly pressure gradient and weak cold advection will bring some gusty winds to the prone gap areas of Washington county overnight into tomorrow morning.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure rose from 1018.4 mb (Thu 12:54) to 1026.0 mb (Fri 09:54) as the ridge builds; it eased 0.5 mb in the last hour, so the rise is levelling off. High pressure and a light gradient favour calm morning and evening windows.

observations.summary: As of 09:35 MST, north flow on the Utah Valley side: Spanish Fork 358° 8 kt gusting 10, Alpine 335° 6 kt gusting 9, Lehi and South Valley Regional light northwest, Provo calm. Salt Lake airport has light south (180° 3 kt), so the transition zone sits north of Point of the Mountain. No south drainage reaches POM. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations. South Valley Regional's latest report is from 08:15 MST, about 2 h old. Add 3–8 kt to valley readings to estimate launch wind.

d1-am.explanation: Today's morning south flow never arrives: the forecast and every Utah Valley station show north wind, which is a tailwind on this south-facing launch. That breaks the usual morning pattern; the northerly gradient behind the departing trough is the cause. Nothing short of the wind backing to 160–200° would change this.

Confirmed winds aloft and a sock steady from the south would make it a go.
